meta.title: Policy Window Monitor — Chile
meta.headline: 7 policy windows are open in Chile: 3 opened by a problem, 4 by politics. Fuel prices opened a new problem window this week.
meta.topicsHeadline: Three windows have no evidence-based alternative in circulation yet, including the new one on fuel prices.
meta.note: Pilot run. The latest week's levels are proposed and await review. A flagged window is a likely opening, not a certainty, and not an endorsement of any proposal.

topics.name: Organised crime & Rules on the Use of Force (RUF)
topics.problem: Crime is the top problem in polls (CEP 57%), with sustained attention.
topics.politics: Level 3 in W5, then 2 after the decision: the mixed-committee report was approved on 7 Oct (Cámara 111–23–5, Senate 29–15–1).
topics.policy: Eight graduated rules, from police presence to lethal force. A bill from the previous government, adopted by this one.
topics.frames: 'Security as a precondition' vs proportionality and human rights. Partially converging.
topics.changed: No new activity. Crime remains a top concern; implementation is the next decision point.
topics.reopen: Implementation controversy or a use-of-force incident

topics.name: Calles sin Violencia replaced by Plan FOCO
topics.problem: Level 2 in W4–W5, then 1 as attention faded. Problem broker: Carolina Tohá, who calls the programme central to reversing the rise in homicides.
topics.politics: The 2027 budget replaces Calles sin Violencia with FOCO. Barrio Prioritario is cut 43.4%; the crime-prevention undersecretariat gets +2.9%.
topics.policy: Two named alternatives compete. Undersecretary Pilar Giannini says FOCO has a stronger design and measurement; no evaluation of either is published.
topics.changed: Under the v0.4 rule this is no longer a window: the problem stream has been weak since W6, so the budget decision on Plan FOCO is moving on politics alone. The Cámara voted the Security budget on 10–12 Nov; results not yet coded.
topics.reopen: A rise in homicides, or an evaluation of either plan

topics.name: Migration: expulsions and detention
topics.problem: Immigration concern fell to 13% (CEP). 1,468 expulsions since March (secondary source).
topics.politics: Law dispatched on 20 Oct (Senate 37–0–1): home entry with a judicial order, re-entry ban raised from 3 to 5 years. Deputies rejected 60-day detention; the President publicly challenged them.
topics.policy: Bill adopted. A separate bill to criminalise irregular entry is pending (stage not verified).
topics.frames: Control and enforcement vs rights. Not assessed in detail.
topics.changed: No new activity.
topics.reopen: Detention reform or irregular-entry offence revived

topics.name: Administrative sentence reductions ('caso Rabat')
topics.problem: Focusing event: 56 reductions for sexual offences against minors, plus reductions for crimes against humanity and for 115 foreign nationals convicted of drug offences. Cadem (27 Oct): 94% reject the reductions; 77% disapprove of the minister's handling.
topics.politics: Undersecretary removed. The minister announced a bill on the Ley 19.856 system and possible revocations. The opposition confirmed a three-chapter constitutional accusation (28 Oct); UDI refused to back it (4 Nov).
topics.policy: The minister advocates a named fix and has access to decision venues. No bill filed.
topics.frames: 'Illegitimate error' vs 'legal compliance'. Partially converging against the reductions.
topics.changed: Cadem (8 Nov): the sentence reductions are the top reason people give for disapproving of the President (43%). The opposition had not filed the constitutional accusation by 12 Nov; parties disagree on timing. Politics stays at 2 because UDI will not back it.

topics.name: Pension funds D and E losses
topics.problem: The Superintendent told the Cámara Labour committee (26 Oct) derivative losses were about US$10.1bn at 30 Sep, easing to about US$7bn by 20 Oct. Fund E −7.56% and Fund D −4.73% year to date. Attention fading after October's rebound.
topics.politics: Sanction process against 7 AFPs opened (20 Oct) and a committee session held. No executive bill.
topics.policy: Compensation and duration limits are mentioned, but no actor meets the entrepreneur definition.
topics.frames: Excessive portfolio duration (regulator) vs systemic failure of individual capitalisation. Not converging.
topics.changed: Fund E rose 8.4% between 24 Oct and 11 Nov. The Cámara admitted the 'Devuelvan la plata' compensation bill (3 Nov); the Superintendent asked to wait for the investigation. Problem stream drops to 1, so the window is closing.
topics.closing: Attention fading as Fund E recovers
topics.reopen: New losses, sanction results, or the compensation bill moving

topics.name: Employment recovery
topics.problem: Unemployment 9.8% (Jul–Sep, INE), highest since 2021; over 1 million unemployed; women 10.5%. Manufacturing jobs −8.1%. Cadem: job-instability worry 71%.
topics.politics: The executive frames Sala Cuna as an employment measure. The SENCE training budget was rejected in the mixed committee.
topics.policy: No dedicated job-creation bill.
topics.changed: Cadem (8 Nov): rising unemployment is the second reason for disapproval (42%) and, with fuel prices, the issue people most want solved. Next INE release around 27 Nov.

topics.name: Sala Cuna Universal (Boletín 14.782-13)
topics.problem: The minister frames female unemployment above 10% and the 20-female-worker threshold (Art. 203) as a hiring barrier.
topics.politics: Senate passage 8 Sep; 'discusión inmediata' urgency 21 Sep; Cámara Labour committee approved it 13–0 (20 Oct) and in particular on 4 Nov, restoring financing (0.30% employer contribution offset by lower unemployment-insurance contributions). Next: Hacienda committee.
topics.policy: Bill with a co-payment subsidy (50% for the most vulnerable 40%, 30% for the 41–60% band; regional source).
topics.frames: Employment for women vs 'negocio' (opposition criticism of the co-payment).
topics.changed: No new step found this week; the bill is in the Cámara Hacienda committee.

topics.name: Budget 2027 and fiscal consolidation
topics.problem: The Fiscal Council (CFA, 28 Oct) warns 2027 revenues may fall short and spending compatible with targets can grow only 0.5% a year, against 1.2% projected.
topics.politics: Budget bill submitted 30 Sep (+1.5% spending). Mood mixed: 58% see spending as inefficient, but only 19% back cutting social programmes (Criteria).
topics.policy: Government austerity path (structural balance −1.8% of GDP); restoration amendments; CFA calls for a fiscal-sustainability agreement.
topics.frames: Fiscal responsibility vs protection of social spending. Not converging.
topics.changed: The Cámara approved the budget in general on 9 Nov and voted 2,242 amendments on 10–12 Nov (results by chapter not yet coded). Senate next; deadline 29–30 Nov. Imacec for September was +0.2%; Q3 GDP is due 18 Nov.

topics.name: Health budget: Ricarte Soto, immunisation, primary care
topics.problem: Senator Juan Luis Castro and health unions oppose the $28,000m Ricarte Soto cut and cuts to vaccines, primary care, mental health, dental and palliative care.
topics.politics: An executive amendment supplemented Ricarte Soto. Health passed 13–11 in the mixed committee; the primary-care programme was rejected.
topics.policy: Restore Ricarte Soto (partly done); raise primary-care per-capita funding without merging programmes; protect immunisation and mental health.
topics.frames: Efficiency vs protection of guaranteed coverage. Not converging.
topics.changed: The government said it will restore rejected funds in the Cámara; primary care had been rejected on a tied vote in the mixed committee. Floor results not yet coded.

topics.name: Surgical waiting lists
topics.problem: Baseline record (Minsal, Q1 2026): 458,109 pending surgeries for 398,496 people, though the median wait fell 40 days. No new data in the period.
topics.politics: No new government action found in the period.
topics.policy: No entrepreneur found in the period.
topics.changed: Quiet; the next Minsal report could move it.

topics.name: Primary-care mental health
topics.problem: Raised only inside the health-budget debate.
topics.politics: Budget line under discussion.
topics.policy: Ideas mentioned, no entrepreneur.
topics.changed: Tied to the health budget vote.

topics.name: Specific excise tax on vapes
topics.problem: No Chilean problem signal in the period. (Colombian vape-tax news excluded.)
topics.politics: Hacienda's precondition, the Reconstruction law, was met with Ley 21.850 on 17 Oct, but no bill was found.
topics.policy: On 16 Jun Hacienda, with Health, said it is drafting a specific tax at rates somewhat below cigarettes; vapes now pay only 19% VAT. U. de Chile specialists back it.
topics.changed: No Chilean signal. The idea is ready, but under v0.4 a topic without problem and politics signals is not a window. Trigger to watch: Hacienda filing the bill.

topics.name: Tobacco contraband and Customs
topics.problem: Revenue gap from contraband estimated by the government at about US$505m.
topics.politics: Ley 21.850 published 17 Oct; a 15.1% Customs budget cut is pending.
topics.policy: Article 10 of the Reconstruction bill: tougher penalties, mandatory criminal complaints by Customs, vehicle seizure (whether kept in the final law: to verify). Sen. Miguel Becker's bill proposes up to 20 years (status not verified).
topics.changed: Customs budget cut still pending in the budget vote.

topics.name: Education budget (SLEP, Yo Elijo Mi PC, Junji/Junaeb)
topics.problem: Programme feedback on SLEP teacher-hour cuts and the end of Yo Elijo Mi PC. Ximena Rubilar called on the President to explain.
topics.politics: Fell from 3 to 2 after the mixed committee rejected the whole Education budget (5 Nov). The government signalled openness to changes.
topics.policy: Restore Yo Elijo Mi PC, liceos bicentenario, learning assessment and SLEP staffing. Entrepreneur set is thin.
entrepreneurs: Opposition members of the mixed committee
topics.changed: Education reached the Cámara floor with its whole chapter rejected; the government announced it would restore funds. Politics stays at 2 because committee arithmetic suggests blocking.

topics.name: CAE/FES student debt
topics.problem: No new problem signal in the period.
topics.politics: The previous government's bill has been in the Senate since August 2025 and stalled in January 2026. Senate Education chair Gustavo Sanhueza (UDI) has raised doubts. No urgency in the period.
topics.policy: Bill in Congress.
topics.changed: Stalled in the Senate.

topics.name: Tolls and electricity tariffs
topics.problem: Cost of living concern; no specific new indicator.
topics.politics: Announcement in W6: Autopista Central toll cut of 10–25% from January 2027 in exchange for a 20-month concession extension; lower electricity prices in 2027. Criteria: 44% oppose the concession mechanism vs 41% in favour.
topics.policy: Adopted by government.
topics.frames: Relief for households vs concession giveaway.
topics.changed: Decided through politics alone. The v0.4 rule would not have flagged it, because the problem stream stayed weak.

topics.name: Regional funding and Ley Cholito
topics.problem: Ley Cholito (responsible pet ownership) line cut 86% ($3,634m to $514m).
topics.politics: Minister of Finance celebrated an agreement with the regional governors on 4 Nov.
topics.policy: Agreement reached.
topics.changed: Agreement with regional governors; decided through politics alone.

topics.name: Storm emergency management
topics.problem: Criteria (25 Oct): the government was the worst-evaluated institution for its storm response.
topics.politics: No formal step.
topics.policy: No idea in circulation.
topics.changed: Attention faded.

topics.problem: No problem signal.
topics.politics: Presidential statement only.
topics.policy: Idea mentioned.
topics.changed: Statement only.

topics.name: Fuel prices and the Mepco stabilisation mechanism
topics.timing: Predictable (weekly price updates; bill under 'discusión inmediata')
topics.problem: Sixth consecutive rise in fuel prices (+$40 per litre from 12 Nov). Gasoline rose 4.5% in October's CPI, which put annual inflation at 4.5%. Cadem (8 Nov): fuel prices and unemployment are the issues people most want the government to solve.
topics.politics: After the extended political committee on 9 Nov, the President announced a bill capping each rise at $20 per litre for 90 days, with 'discusión inmediata' urgency and the backing of governing-party presidents and bench heads. Reactions in Congress were mixed.
topics.policy: Executive bill to change Mepco; Hacienda considering fiscal savings to moderate rises. Bonuses for taxi drivers, school transport and artisanal fishers were extended in September.
topics.frames: 'Social urgency' (President) vs 'fuel is still cheap for the region' (Minister Mas).
topics.changed: New topic this week. Entered through the discovery net: a coverage spike plus poll salience.

ideas: Sala Cuna fund financed by a 0.30% employer contribution offset by lower unemployment-insurance contributions
bills: Boletín 14.782-13, second stage; Cámara Hacienda committee next
T07.evidenceNote: Meta-analyses find more childcare raises maternal employment; Chilean primary studies on the Art. 203 mandate exist. Co-payment design: primary studies, no synthesis.

T08.evidenceNote: Meta-analyses on fiscal rules and deficits. Which cuts do the least harm: no synthesis found.

ideas: Raise primary-care per-capita funding without merging programmes
T09.evidenceNote: Reviews on primary-care strengthening and immunisation uptake. Cuts to high-cost coverage: no synthesis found.

entrepreneurs: Opposition members of the mixed committee
T14.evidenceNote: Hardware-only programmes show small learning effects; pedagogy-linked software does better. SLEP staffing: no evidence found.

ideas: Keep the place-based Calles sin Violencia model
T02.evidenceNote: Campbell reviews on hot-spots policing and focused deterrence show crime reductions. Neither plan has a published impact evaluation; one released before 30 Nov could discriminate between them.

ideas: Exclude sexual crimes against minors and crimes against humanity
T04.evidenceNote: No synthesis on administrative sentence-reduction regimes; reviews exist on sex-offender treatment and recidivism. No evidence-based alternative in this window.

T05.evidenceNote: Primary studies on default and life-cycle funds; no synthesis on derivative-risk limits; no evidence found on compensation. This window lacks a viable alternative.

T06.evidenceNote: Meta-analyses of active labour-market programmes. No hiring subsidy proposed.

ideas: Specific vape tax set below cigarette rates
T12.evidenceNote: IARC Handbook vol. 14: sufficient evidence that tobacco taxes prevent initiation and uptake among young people. Trigger: Hacienda filing the bill.

Use fiscal savings to moderate rises
Targeted bonuses for transport and fishing sectors (extended in September)
bills: Mepco bill announced 9 Nov with 'discusión inmediata'; filing not verified by 12 Nov
Bonus extension bill (sent to the Cámara 30 Sep)
T21.evidence: Reviews exist on fuel subsidies; none found on price-smoothing funds
T21.evidenceNote: Cross-country work on energy subsidies finds general fuel-price support is regressive and costly compared with targeted transfers. No synthesis found on price-smoothing funds such as Mepco.

calendar.label: Hacienda committee and floor; target before Feb

context.executive: President José Antonio Kast (Partido Republicano), in office since 11 March 2026.
context.approvalNote: Cadem: approval fell from 35% (September average) to 26% on 1 Nov, then rose to 29% on 8 Nov. Criteria fell to 24% on 8 Nov. The two polls moved in opposite directions this week.
problems: Cadem (8 Nov): unemployment and fuel prices are the issues people most want the government to solve.
Cadem (8 Nov): reasons for disapproval: sentence reductions 43%, rising unemployment 42%.
CEP 96 priorities: crime 57%, health 42%, education 28%, drug trafficking 28%, pensions 18%.
context.budget: Budget Law 2027: the mixed committee dispatched it on 6 Nov with Education and Science rejected. The Cámara approved it in general on 9 Nov and voted 2,242 amendments on 10–12 Nov. Senate 17–19 Nov; deadline 29–30 Nov.
context.cabinet: The President joined an extended political committee on 9 Nov and announced the fuel bill afterwards. He travels to China on 14 Nov. No cabinet change.

steps: Collected W9 (6–12 Nov) from the Chile source log: news, radio and TV sites, polls, official statistics and Congress news.
Coded each item to a topic, a stream and one concept, with its context (programme, speaker) and a short quote where one supports the code.
Weighed concepts by corroboration across independent sources in the same week.
Proposed problem and politics levels for every topic, with a rationale, and listed them in the Review tab.
Re-rated W1–W8 under v0.4: the policy level was dropped from the weekly grid and windows were re-flagged with the two-stream rule.
Added one topic (fuel prices) through the discovery net.
method.volume: 109 coded items in total; 21 new in W9.
rules: A potential window is flagged when the problem and politics streams are both at level 2 or 3 in the same week.
Whichever stream reached level 2 first sets the coupling: problem window (consequential) or political window (doctrinal).
The politics level is lowered by one when approval or national mood is clearly against the move, or when coalition arithmetic suggests blocking.
Executive signals take precedence over congressional ones.
A level carries forward up to two weeks without new items, then drops one level.
The policy stream is checked only for topics where a window has been flagged.
limitations: W9 levels are proposed and await human review (Review tab). Earlier weeks were rated by one analyst without double coding.
Floor results of the Cámara budget votes (10–12 Nov) were not yet available by chapter when this run was coded.
Audio and video sources (talk shows, podcasts, radio) were read through their written coverage; no transcription yet.
El Mercurio is behind a full paywall; La Tercera and El País are metered.
Evidence states in policy checks come from analyst knowledge and need verification in Epistemonikos, Cochrane, Campbell or 3ie.
validation: Sala Cuna, Rules on the Use of Force and expulsions were flagged before their decisions. Pass.
Sentence reductions detected in W7, within 7 days. Pass.

The v0.4 two-stream rule would not have flagged tolls (T16) and regional funding (T17), both decided through politics alone with a weak problem stream. Politics-only decisions are a known blind spot of the rule.
Calles sin Violencia → FOCO moves from 'open' (v0.3) to 'watch' (v0.4): the budget decision is going ahead without public attention.
nextVersion: Version 2: prediction — how stories are being prepared and how coverage will shift the agenda (journalists as a user group).
Read Cámara and Senate records directly for votes by chapter.
Transcribe the weekly political review programmes.

reviews.label: 6–12 Nov
reviews.note: First run under Protocol v0.4. All topics re-rated on problem and politics only; earlier weeks re-labelled under the v0.4 window rule. W9 levels are proposed and await review.

signals.rationale: A sixth consecutive price rise and gasoline's jump in October's CPI are indicator changes, corroborated by three sources. Cadem places fuel prices among the issues people most want solved, which meets the 'top concern' test for level 3.

The executive announced a bill with 'discusión inmediata', the strongest urgency, after agreeing it with governing-party leaders. Approval is low, but mood favours action on fuel prices, so no level is deducted. Problem came first (Cadem 8 Nov, bill 9 Nov), so this is a problem window.
The sentence reductions remain the top reason for disapproving of the President, a sign that attention is sustained.
The accusation is announced but not filed, the opposition disagrees on timing, and UDI will not support it. A formal step is pending, but the coalition arithmetic suggests blocking, so it stays at 2.
Fund E has recovered strongly since late October and coverage has fallen. With the problem stream below 2, the window is marked as closing (attention fading).
The compensation bill was admitted and the sanction process continues; a formal step exists, so politics stays at 2.
Unemployment is a leading reason for disapproval and the top concern in Cadem, corroborated by two outlets.
The Cámara approved the budget in general and voted on amendments: decisive use of the budget tool with a scheduled deadline.
Weak growth (Imacec +0.2%, Q3 likely negative) keeps the fiscal problem at signal level.
The executive announced restoration amendments for rejected health and education funds.
Education reached the floor rejected. A restoration is promised (level 3 step), lowered by one because the committee vote suggests it could be blocked again.
Polls diverge: Cadem 29% (+3), Criteria 24% (−1). Approval stays low but is not moving sharply, so no topic's politics level is lowered on approval grounds this week.

discovery.text: Fuel prices: coverage spike across six logged outlets plus Cadem salience → entered as T21.
Inflation (CPI 4.5%) and growth (Imacec +0.2%) are tracked as indicators inside T21 and T08 rather than as separate topics.
